# Deloitte

## Executive summary
Deloitte is the world's largest professional services network, with US$70.5 billion in revenue for fiscal 2025 and clients that include nearly 90% of the Fortune 500. It sells AI strategy, governance, assurance and change work as one part of a very wide audit, tax and consulting catalogue. It wins on brand safety, global scale and bundled services, and it sells mainly through large, negotiated, project-based engagements.

## Firmographics
- **Website:** https://www.deloitte.com (US site: https://www.deloitte.com/us/en.html)
- **HQ:** London, England, UK (Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited, founded 1845). US HQ: Not found.
- **Size:**
  - Revenue of US$70.5 billion for the year ending 31 May 2025.
  - Workforce of over 470,000.
  - Ownership: member firms of a private company limited by guarantee, incorporated in England and Wales. There is no public funding or listing.
  - FY2026: one third-party blog reports US$74.5 billion and nearly 500,000 people. I did not verify this on Deloitte's own site.
- **Primary target:**
  - Large enterprises. Nearly 90% of the Fortune 500 and more than 9,000 US-based private companies.
  - Mid-market and family firms via Deloitte Private, for privately held businesses, family enterprises and emerging growth companies.
  - Industries on the US site include consumer, energy, financial services, government, life sciences and health care, and technology, media and telecom.

## Positioning
- **Hero message:** The US homepage currently shows "Connecting the dots. That's how progress happens." The page title is "Deloitte US | Together Makes Progress". A rotating banner above it features a finance leader survey. The AI governance page headline is "Unlock the potential of AI while protecting what matters most".
- **Problem they claim to solve (AI):** Teams move fast on AI but lack a single, defensible way to govern it end to end. They also claim to avoid governing too little, which invites risk, or governing too much, which slows adoption.
- **Category they claim:** Trustworthy AI™, a branded framework. It is an integrated approach to building AI that is safe, secure, compliant and scalable.
- **Recent messaging shifts:**
  - In FY2025 Deloitte completed a new storefront and go-to-market strategy that groups its capabilities into more integrated solutions.
  - In August 2026 it expanded AI Controls and Assurance services to help organizations adopt, scale and govern AI.
  - The launch pitch cites a gap between ambition and assurance. 74% of companies plan to deploy agentic AI within two years, but only 21% report a mature governance model for autonomous agents.

## Core features
| Offer | Outcome promised |
|---|---|
| AI risk management and governance program | Controls across the AI lifecycle, clear accountability, regulatory tracking and audit-ready evidence, for faster delivery with more trust. |
| AI Controls and Assurance | AI risk assessments, model validations and redesigned controls, especially where AI affects financial reporting. |
| ISO 42001 and readiness services | Readiness evaluations, AI model testing, governance, risk and compliance program development, tooling and talent. |
| Human Trust with AI | Workforce impact analysis, reskilling and training, culture and leadership readiness, and internal change management. |
| AI strategy and workshops | AI strategy development, specialized delivery teams, and workshops where teams explore practical use cases and prototypes. |

## Pricing and packaging
- **Model:** Custom, negotiated engagements. Deloitte does not publish standard rate cards, and pricing is negotiated case by case. Engagements are commonly billed hourly, with rates varying by role.
- **Entry price:** Not public. Third-party estimates only:
  - Vendr: blended rates typically $200 to $800 per hour depending on team and geography.
  - Velocity (a competing AI firm, so treat as biased): $300 to $600 per hour, with AI advisory engagements starting at about $250,000.
  - Public-sector example: Deloitte's own US GSA price sheet lists $373.00 per hour for a consulting management executive.
- **Packaging:** Project-based work with milestones, plus managed "Operate" services listed on the US site. No self-serve tier.

## Market sentiment
Client reviews of Deloitte's AI governance work: Not found. The sources below are employee reviews and news coverage.
- **What users love:**
  - Reputation and scale. A consulting employee wrote "Good company reputation and huge connections" (Glassdoor, Sept 2026, employee review).
  - Industry standing. Gartner ranked Deloitte the No. 1 consulting service provider worldwide by revenue for the eighth consecutive year.
- **What users complain about:**
  - Cost versus output. A 1-star reviewer wrote that "the client will pay the big bucks to get Excel lists and meetings" (Management Consulted, quoting Glassdoor, employee review, not a client).
  - AI quality. In 2025 Deloitte Australia agreed to refund part of the AU$440,000 it was paid for a government report with apparent AI-generated errors, including fabricated legal quotations and non-existent academic papers. The revised report disclosed that Azure OpenAI was used. Reports state the fee as AU$440,000 or about US$290,000, which is the same amount in two currencies.
  - Staffing. Employees report long hours and low pay in Glassdoor summaries. This is a delivery risk signal, not client feedback.

## Go-to-market
- **Channels:**
  - Thought leadership: Deloitte Insights and the "State of AI in the Enterprise" report.
  - Webcasts: Dbriefs webcasts.
  - Social: LinkedIn, X, YouTube and Instagram.
  - Press releases for new AI services.
  - Case studies.
- **Partners:** Alliance pages for AWS, Google, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow and Workday.
- **Sales motion:**
  - Enterprise relationships and a public "Submit RFP" page.
  - Third-party analysis describes AI pricing as RFP-by-RFP and partner-controlled.
  - AI governance is cross-sold from audit, risk and assurance relationships.

## Where they are weak
- **No public pricing.** Buyers cannot see a price or a scope before a sales conversation (Vendr).
- **Audit independence limits.** Deloitte's own legal footer says certain services may not be available to attest clients under public accounting rules.
- **Public AI quality failure.** The Australian report refund (Oct 2025) is a documented, widely covered case. It sits awkwardly next to a "Trustworthy AI" claim.
- **Enterprise-shaped offer.** Its AI governance pages talk about portfolio-level oversight, platforms, tooling and regulatory tracking. There is no stated offer for small or mid-size executive teams (Not found on the pages reviewed).
- **Long timelines.** Competitor Velocity claims implementation programs typically take 6 to 18 months. This is an unverified competitor claim.
- **Team shape is not named on the page.** The AI governance and assurance pages do not name the person who will lead the work (Not found). Whether a named senior advisor is Acme Advisory's edge is an inference, not a sourced fact.
